statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-58076 (GHSA-8prw-8m6x-8w6f): in Apache Airflow 3.3.0, BaseSerialization.deserialize rebuilt exception nodes by importing a class name taken from the serialized data, so a Dag author could make the Scheduler or API server import and call an arbitrary callable through an operator's executor_config. Airflow 3.3.1 fixes it (https://lists.apache.org/thread/t81p688t15jozxsng8521o60nh2kfsos, https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/68511): airflow/serialization/serialized_objects.py gains _resolve_airflow_exception, which accepts only an already loaded AirflowException subclass, and a fixed table of builtin exceptions. The advisory affects only Airflow 3.3.0, and no earlier Airflow release was published as this package. We read all 58 airflow packages for Debian 13 published in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-28, 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-17, amd64 and arm64 (116 package files). For every package we read its md5sums manifest, which lists every file the package installs with its digest, and matched the digests of the files that carry the fix against the same files in the released wheels on PyPI; we also unpacked the amd64 and arm64 packages of 3.3.0-0, 3.3.2-19, 3.4.0-0 and 3.4.0-17. Both architectures ship the same copy of those files in every version. 3.3.0-0 to 3.3.0-3 install Airflow 3.3.0, 3.3.1-0 to 3.3.1-15 install 3.3.1, 3.3.2-0 to 3.3.2-19 install 3.3.2 and 3.4.0-0 to 3.4.0-17 install 3.4.0, each with one copy of the file. In 3.3.0-0 to 3.3.0-3 serialized_objects.py is byte for byte the file in the apache-airflow-core 3.3.0 wheel and has no _resolve_airflow_exception. From 3.3.1-0 to 3.3.2-19 it is byte for byte the apache-airflow-core 3.3.1 wheel's, which defines and calls _resolve_airflow_exception; 3.4.0-0 to 3.4.0-17 ship one digest of the file, and the unpacked 3.4.0-17 copy defines and calls it too. 3.3.1-0 is the first published package with the fix.
